1. What the code shows (settled by reading it):
(a) Muon applies no weight decay. muon_update renormalizes filters to norm sqrt(out) every step. So all wd effects, including E016's +0.24 pp, came from the SGD groups. H1.5.4 is settled.
(b) Newton-Schulz already runs 3 steps, so the NS-iteration lever is spent.
(c) The images already travel to the GPU as uint8 and are normalized there. Part (1) of I053 is already done.
(d) The whitening bias gets lr 0 after 3 epochs (75/219 steps, about 34%), but it keeps requires_grad. Its full-resolution backward (whitening GELU backward and group-1 conv1 input-grad) still runs for the rest of training.

2. Chaotic decorrelation, confirmed by E029, E030 and E032. Any change to the dynamics re-rolls the per-seed outcomes. Each such change resets the tip to about 0.7526 (the population mean) plus the idea's own effect, with about 0.15 pp SD on the 3-seed mean. Time-neutral boosters have a negative mean effect: label smoothing, averaging and warm-up changes run from −0.2 to −0.6 pp. The airbench schedule sits at a sharp optimum. The weight knobs (wd, LS level, Muon lr) are flat, and the timing knobs are sharp.

3. Unexplained excess time savings, a mechanism nobody has proposed yet:
- E028: freezing 25% of steps saved 0.84 s. That is about 15 ms per truncated step, more than half of a ~27 ms 32 px step, for 20% of the conv MACs.
- E031: cutting 20 steps saved 0.95 s, about 47 ms per removed step, twice the average step.
Per-pixel GEMM cost doesn't explain either. Candidates:
(i) Part of each step is bound by parameter or launch overhead (eager fused SGD, a separate Muon cudagraph, Python LR loops, Lookahead foreach over all params and buffers on 4 CPUs).
(ii) Large-map memory traffic (BN, GELU, pool backward at 31×31).
(iii) Those variants also warmed more code paths in build, which removed trial-0 first-call costs.
So any lever that removes stem backward or whole steps pays about 1.5–2× what my MAC model says. My time forecasts have repeatedly come in too high, so I now lean low.

4. Resolution. Early low resolution is nearly free (E026). A late or abrupt jump into 32 px is costly (E011, E018, E024).

5. Epoch dial. Each 0.25 epoch is worth about 0.14 s and 0.12 pp. Stacked on the freeze, it is the obvious path: the freeze buys about 0.8 s for about 0.1–0.2 pp, which beats the dial's rate by about 3×.

6. Noise:
- 3-seed mean: SD about 0.15 pp.
- 10-seed held-out mean: SE about 0.08 pp.
- A rebuild shifts the mean by about 0.03–0.05 pp.
- Seeds 3–12 carry a winner's curse after about 10 keep decisions.

Unsure:
- Whether the excess savings come from host overhead (which would argue for capturing the whole step, optimizer included, in one graph) or from memory bandwidth.
- PCIe transfer, which matters more if the levers are bandwidth-bound.

structured_output.world_model:
W5 (contrarian), after E032. Tip E027: 8.75 epochs, 219 steps, 20/24/28/32 px at 0/15/40/70% of steps. It runs 5.878 s and scores 0.7547 on seeds 0–2, but only about 0.7526 on held-out seeds, which is below the 0.753 bar.

1. What the code shows (settled by reading it):
(a) Muon applies no weight decay. muon_update renormalizes filters to norm sqrt(out) every step. So all wd effects, including E016's +0.24 pp, came from the SGD groups. H1.5.4 is settled.
(b) Newton-Schulz already runs 3 steps, so the NS-iteration lever is spent.
(c) The images already travel to the GPU as uint8 and are normalized there. Part (1) of I053 is already done.
(d) The whitening bias gets lr 0 after 3 epochs (75/219 steps, about 34%), but it keeps requires_grad. Its full-resolution backward (whitening GELU backward and group-1 conv1 input-grad) still runs for the rest of training.

2. Chaotic decorrelation, confirmed by E029, E030 and E032. Any change to the dynamics re-rolls the per-seed outcomes. Each such change resets the tip to about 0.7526 (the population mean) plus the idea's own effect, with about 0.15 pp SD on the 3-seed mean. Time-neutral boosters have a negative mean effect: label smoothing, averaging and warm-up changes run from −0.2 to −0.6 pp. The airbench schedule sits at a sharp optimum. The weight knobs (wd, LS level, Muon lr) are flat, and the timing knobs are sharp.

3. Unexplained excess time savings, a mechanism nobody has proposed yet:
- E028: freezing 25% of steps saved 0.84 s. That is about 15 ms per truncated step, more than half of a ~27 ms 32 px step, for 20% of the conv MACs.
- E031: cutting 20 steps saved 0.95 s, about 47 ms per removed step, twice the average step.
Per-pixel GEMM cost doesn't explain either. Candidates:
(i) Part of each step is bound by parameter or launch overhead (eager fused SGD, a separate Muon cudagraph, Python LR loops, Lookahead foreach over all params and buffers on 4 CPUs).
(ii) Large-map memory traffic (BN, GELU, pool backward at 31×31).
(iii) Those variants also warmed more code paths in build, which removed trial-0 first-call costs.
So any lever that removes stem backward or whole steps pays about 1.5–2× what my MAC model says. My time forecasts have repeatedly come in too high, so I now lean low.

4. Resolution. Early low resolution is nearly free (E026). A late or abrupt jump into 32 px is costly (E011, E018, E024).

5. Epoch dial. Each 0.25 epoch is worth about 0.14 s and 0.12 pp. Stacked on the freeze, it is the obvious path: the freeze buys about 0.8 s for about 0.1–0.2 pp, which beats the dial's rate by about 3×.

6. Noise:
- 3-seed mean: SD about 0.15 pp.
- 10-seed held-out mean: SE about 0.08 pp.
- A rebuild shifts the mean by about 0.03–0.05 pp.
- Seeds 3–12 carry a winner's curse after about 10 keep decisions.

Unsure:
- Whether the excess savings come from host overhead (which would argue for capturing the whole step, optimizer included, in one graph) or from memory bandwidth.
- PCIe transfer, which matters more if the levers are bandwidth-bound.
- Whether a held-out mean near 0.7545 is safe against the 40-seed bar of 0.75. I think yes.

forecasts.reason: Freeze is ~-0.82 s on this base; +12 steps add ~0.27 s. Easily under 5.75 s; +0.5 epoch roughly offsets the freeze loss, so held-out ~0.754-0.755.
uint8 GPU transfer is already in the code; only the trial-0 eigh/alloc warm-up remains, worth ≤0.05 s on the mean. Math is identical, so the per-seed results are kept.

Whitening bias lr is 0 after 34%, but its 31x31 backward still runs. Detaching it pays more than its MAC share (E028 pattern); the bias stops a bit earlier, so accuracy is ~neutral but re-rolled to the population mean.
~35 more truncated steps save ~0.3 s; freezing the stem earlier at mid-LR likely costs 0.1-0.2 pp, right at the 0.15 pp gate.
No recipe change, so the row reproduces the tip. Fresh seeds likely regress below seeds 3-12 (winner's curse), and the pooled mean is <0.753 for the E027 tip.
Forward-only BN stats on group 1 are a small part of a truncated step (<2%). A train-to-eval BN switch from one batch at momentum 0.6 shifts downstream activations, risking 0.1-0.3 pp.
Muon's fixed-norm orthogonalized updates are the main short-run accelerator; SGD at batch 2000 with airbench scaling should lose ≥0.3 pp. NS removal saves ~3%.
E028's outsized saving implies BN/GELU/pool kernels on the 31x31 maps carry ≥30% of GPU time, with whitening plus group 1 ≥35% of the step.

cruxes: Why did E028 (~15 ms per truncated step) and E031 (~47 ms per removed step) save far more than per-pixel step cost predicts? Is it host/launch overhead (eager fused SGD, a separate Muon graph, Python LR loops, Lookahead foreach), memory bandwidth, or extra build warm-up? If it is host overhead, capturing the whole step (optimizer + Lookahead) in one graph is a bit-identical lever worth several percent.
What is I052's held-out seeds 3–12 mean? It decides whether freeze + epoch top-up becomes the new base for all stem levers (I054/I055/I057).
Does the whitening-bias backward detach (I054) cost any accuracy, given that the bias already stops at 34% of steps?
